related_questions.question: Can you have COVID and still test negative?

text_blocks.snippet: Yes, it is possible to have COVID-19 and still test negative, especially with antigen tests. Factors like the type of test used, timing of the test in relation to symptom onset, and viral load can influence test results.

list.title: Test Type:
list.snippet: Molecular tests, like PCR, are generally more sensitive than antigen tests, which are often used for rapid, at-home testing.

list.title: Timing:
list.snippet: If you test too early in the course of infection, the viral load may not be high enough to be detected by the test.

list.title: Viral Load:
list.snippet: Some individuals may not have a high enough viral load to trigger a positive result, even if they are infected, especially with antigen tests.

list.title: Other Infections:
list.snippet: It's also possible to have symptoms from other respiratory illnesses, like influenza or RSV, while testing negative for COVID-19, according to the University of Nebraska Medical Center.

related_questions.question: What does the very beginning of COVID feel like?

text_blocks.snippet: The initial symptoms of COVID-19 can feel similar to a mild cold or other respiratory illnesses, with possible symptoms like fatigue, sore throat, and mild cough. Some individuals might also experience a headache or fever. The severity of symptoms can vary widely, and it's important to be mindful of even mild symptoms as they can potentially worsen.

related_questions.question: What feels like COVID but isn't?
related_questions.snippet: Like flu and COVID-19, colds are also caused by viruses and can be passed to others. Symptoms of a cold tend to be mild. You may have a runny nose, cough, congestion, and sore throat. But you won't usually have the aches and fever that are common with COVID-19 and flu.

text_blocks.snippet: Possible Reasons for COVID Symptoms with a Negative Test:

list.title: Early infection:
list.snippet: The virus may still be in its early stages of replication, and the test may not detect it yet.

list.title: Incorrect test use:
list.snippet: The test may not have been performed correctly, or the sample may not have been collected properly.

list.title: False negative result:
list.snippet: Even with a properly performed test, there is a small chance of getting a false negative result.

list.title: Other underlying conditions:
list.snippet: Symptoms may be caused by other underlying conditions, such as the flu, a common cold, or allergies.

list.title: Delayed viral shedding:
list.snippet: In some cases, the virus can continue to be shed in small amounts after a person has recovered, even if they test negative.
If you have COVID symptoms and test negative, it is important to isolate yourself and monitor your symptoms closely.
Get tested again: if your symptoms worsen or do not improve after a few days.
Contact your healthcare provider: if you have concerns about your symptoms or if you are at high risk for complications from COVID-19.
Follow public health guidelines: such as wearing masks, washing your hands frequently, and avoiding close contact with others.

text_blocks.snippet: Note: It is important to remember that a negative COVID test does not completely rule out the possibility of having COVID-19. If you have symptoms that are consistent with COVID-19, it is always best to err on the side of caution and take appropriate measures.
